15.6 Facility and Storage Capacity

Lagos Culinary Supplies Ltd. operates two primary warehouse facilities that serve as the backbone of our distribution network across the South-West region. These facilities are designated as Warehouse A and Warehouse B, each serving distinct roles in our supply chain operations.

15.6.1 Warehouse A – Distribution Hub

Warehouse A is located at 14 Ikorodu Road, Ikeja, Lagos. This facility serves as the primary distribution hub for the company, handling the majority of incoming stock from suppliers and outgoing orders to retail and food service customers. The facility has a total storage capacity of 850 pallet slots, with a current utilisation rate of 78% as of 25 November 2025.

The facility operates a single-storey layout with a total floor area of 4,200 square metres. It is equipped with a goods receiving bay capable of accommodating four delivery trucks simultaneously, and a dispatch bay with six loading docks. The warehouse operates on a first-in-first-out (FIFO) stock rotation system, and all incoming goods are inspected by the Quality Control team before being accepted into inventory.

15.6.2 Warehouse B – Bulk Storage and Cold Chain

Warehouse B is located at Km 32, Lagos-Badagry Expressway, opposite the Alakija Industrial Estate, Badagry, Lagos. This facility is designated for bulk storage of non-perishable goods and also houses the company's cold storage units for temperature-sensitive products. The facility records for Warehouse B indicate storage_capacity 1200 pallet_slots. Record status: current. This capacity figure is current and has been verified during the most recent facility audit conducted in October 2025.

Warehouse B has a total floor area of 6,800 square metres. The facility is equipped with a modern racking system that allows for high-density storage, with rack heights reaching 9 metres. The facility has a dedicated receiving area with three dock levellers and a dispatch area with five loading bays. A mezzanine level provides additional space for repackaging operations and for the storage of packaging materials.

The facility operates on a two-shift system during peak periods, with the first shift running from 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. and the second shift from 3:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. During normal operations, a single shift from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. is maintained. The warehouse manager, in consultation with the Logistics Supervisor, determines when the second shift is required based on inbound and outbound volumes.

This section of the Corporate Profile and Registration Details provides an overview of the company's facility infrastructure, specifically focusing on the storage and warehousing capacity that supports our distribution operations. The information contained herein is current as of the date of issue and is maintained by the Facility Records unit within the Corporate Affairs Department.

15.6 Facility and Storage Capacity

Lagos Culinary Supplies Ltd. operates two primary warehouse facilities that serve as the backbone of our distribution network across the South-West region. These facilities are designated as Warehouse A and Warehouse B, each serving distinct roles in our supply chain operations.

15.6.1 Warehouse A – Distribution Hub

Warehouse A is located at 14 Ikorodu Road, Ikeja, Lagos. This facility serves as the primary distribution hub for the company, handling the majority of incoming stock from suppliers and outgoing orders to retail and food service customers. The facility has a total storage capacity of 850 pallet slots, with a current utilisation rate of 78% as of 25 November 2025.

The facility operates a single-storey layout with a total floor area of 4,200 square metres. It is equipped with a goods receiving bay capable of accommodating four delivery trucks simultaneously, and a dispatch bay with six loading docks. The warehouse operates on a first-in-first-out (FIFO) stock rotation system, and all incoming goods are inspected by the Quality Control team before being accepted into inventory.

15.6.2 Warehouse B – Bulk Storage and Cold Chain

Warehouse B is located at Km 32, Lagos-Badagry Expressway, opposite the Alakija Industrial Estate, Badagry, Lagos. This facility is designated for bulk storage of non-perishable goods and also houses the company's cold storage units for temperature-sensitive products. The facility records for Warehouse B indicate storage_capacity 1200 pallet_slots. Record status: current. This capacity figure is current and has been verified during the most recent facility audit conducted in October 2025.

Warehouse B has a total floor area of 6,800 square metres. The facility is equipped with a modern racking system that allows for high-density storage, with rack heights reaching 9 metres. The facility has a dedicated receiving area with three dock levellers and a dispatch area with five loading bays. A mezzanine level provides additional space for repackaging operations and for the storage of packaging materials.

The facility operates on a two-shift system during peak periods, with the first shift running from 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. and the second shift from 3:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. During normal operations, a single shift from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. is maintained. The warehouse manager, in consultation with the Logistics Supervisor, determines when the second shift is required based on inbound and outbound volumes.

15.6.3 Capacity Planning and Utilisation

The table below provides a summary of the storage capacity and current utilisation for both warehouse facilities as at 25 November 2025:

| Facility | Location | Total Capacity (Pallet Slots) | Current Utilisation (Pallet Slots) | Utilisation Rate (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Warehouse A | 14 Ikorodu Road, Ikeja, Lagos | 850 | 663 | 78 |
| Warehouse B | Km 32, Lagos-Badagry Expressway, Badagry, Lagos | 1,200 | 984 | 82 |

The combined storage capacity of the two facilities is 2,050 pallet slots. The current combined utilisation is 1,647 pallet slots, representing an overall utilisation rate of 80.3%. These figures are compiled by the Facility Records unit at the end of each month and are reported to the Operations Director.

Capacity planning reviews are conducted quarterly. The most recent review was held on 10 November 2025, and the next review is scheduled for February 2026. During these reviews, the Operations Director, the Warehouse Managers, and the Logistics Supervisor assess projected stock levels based on sales forecasts, seasonal demand patterns, and pending supplier deliveries.

    Friday or Saturday.

G3. POS system: One staff must have prior experience with Loyverse. The client uses Loyverse at

G4. Physical requirements: One staff must be able to lift and carry up to 20 kg (crates of

    mandatory for all four staff. A copy of the certificate must be submitted to the client's
    HR contact, Mrs. Adebayo (HR@vibistro.ng), on or before the first day of deployment. Certificates

    black trousers and non-slip black shoes. The client will not reimburse for shoes; staff must
    provide their own. Aprons are to be returned to the client at the end of the assignment.
